title: Add downgrade guard and integrated backup/restore to private installer upgrade tooling
author: Evelyn Park
body: Background and motivation: Private deployments require safe, predictable upgrades and the ability to recover or rollback when things go wrong. This PR adds a downgrade guard, an integrated backup/restore flow, and stronger version-pinning to the private installer upgrade tooling (CLI + Helm hooks + Terraform artifacts). The goal is to make upgrades reversible where possible, block unsupported downgrades proactively, and provide a reproducible snapshot/restore path for incidents. Changes included: 1) Installer CLI: new subcommands 'redwood-installer backup', 'redwood-installer restore', and an enhanced 'redwood-installer upgrade --allow-downgrade' gated by an explicit flag. Backups are written to the configured object store and annotated with schema_version, installer_version, and a cryptographic checksum. 2) Downgrade guard: before performing a downgrade the installer compares current DB schema version vs target version and consults a downgrade-compatibility table. If a downgrade is unsafe (irreversible migration or incompatible data transforms), the installer fails fast with a clear message and a pointer to documented mitigations. 3) Version pinning: the upgrade planner now enforces adjacency rules for minor/patch upgrades for schema migrations; cross-major upgrades require an explicit migration plan and 'force' flag. 4) Helm: added pre-upgrade and post-upgrade hooks to run DB dump and post-migration verification jobs (jobs/backup-job.yaml, jobs/verify-migration.yaml). Hook behavior is opt-in via chart values and disabled by default for air-gapped installs until object store config is present. 5) Terraform: module now emits a stable snapshot_metadata resource (S3 key + kms_key_id) used by the installer to find/verify backups; added IAM policy snippets to module outputs to help customers grant the installer least-privilege access. 6) Schema migration tooling: migration registry updated to record reverse_migration scripts when available; migrations without reverses are marked in the compatibility table. 7) Docs & examples: upgrade playbook, rollback runbook, and sample backup/restore commands added to docs/private/upgrade.md. Checklist: - [x] CLI commands implemented and unit-tested - [x] Helm hooks and chart values added - [x] Terraform outputs added and documented - [x] Integration tests (happy path backup/restore) - [x] E2E upgrade test in perf-canary - [x] Docs and runbooks updated - [x] Safety gating and feature flagging for air-gapped installs Testing and verification: Ran local integration tests against a test Postgres cluster and a minio object store. Performed an end-to-end upgrade from v1.8.2 -> v1.9.0 (minor upgrade) and validated no data loss, successful post-migration verifications, and a successful restore from the backup snapshot. Also validated that attempting to downgrade from v1.9.0 -> v1.8.2 without '--allow-downgrade' blocks the operation with the expected error. Rollback behavior: If a post-upgrade verification job fails, installer triggers an automatic restore from the latest successful pre-upgrade backup (configurable behavior). For safe downgrades where a reverse migration script exists, the installer will run the reverse migration and verify integrity; otherwise the downgrade is blocked. Migration safety table: included compatibility metadata mapping migration ids -> reversible:true|false and notes for operators. Backwards compatibility and operator experience: Default behavior remains conservative (no automatic downgrades) to protect customer data. Operators who accept the risk can opt-in via explicit flags and documented steps. Security: Backups are encrypted using the configured KMS key and the installer verifies object checksums before restoring. IAM recommendations are included. Rollout plan: Merge to main and ship in the 2026.03 private-installer release. We will gate the Helm hook defaults behind the chart value and communicate to customers via the release notes and upgrade runbook. Related: ENG-4321 adds further telemetry for migration runs; SUP-1289 tracked a recent support case where a customer attempted an unsupported downgrade.
commits: add: backup/restore CLI and integration tests; add: downgrade guard logic and compatibility table; add: helm pre/post upgrade hooks; add: terraform snapshot_metadata output; fix: unit tests and lint failures; docs: upgrade and rollback runbooks; chore: bump installer version to v1.9.0
review_comments: Ava Chen: Please add a safety feature flag to opt-in Helm hooks for air-gapped installs. - Addressed in charts/private/values.yaml (values.backupHooks.enabled=false by default)

Diego Morales: Can we record reverse_migration scripts in the registry when available? That will make automated downgrades safer. - Added reverse_script references and compatibility notes in migration_registry.go
Priya Nair: Add more unit tests around checksum verification and KMS encryption paths. - Tests added in tests/integration/backup_restore_test.go
Diego Morales: CI failed on lint initially; noticed a long function in migration_registry.go. Please split and add comments. - Refactored into helper functions and added comments, lint now passes
ci_details: CI: installer unit tests (passed), integration (flaky on first run - minio startup timeout), lint (failed -> fixed), e2e-perf-canary (passed). One rerun required for integration due to timing; final status: pass. Pipeline: ci/installer-pipeline.yml uses matrix for Go versions and runs helm lint, terraform validate, and integration suite.
release_notes: private-installer: Add backup/restore commands, downgrade guard, and_version pinning for safer upgrades. Backups are stored encrypted and annotated with schema and installer versions. Helm pre/post upgrade hooks available via chart value. See docs/private/upgrade.md for full rollback and migration playbooks.
test_plan: Unit tests for CLI and registry; integration tests against Postgres+MinIO; e2e upgrade in perf-canary. Validation steps included pre-upgrade backup, post-migration verification, and restore verification. Manual smoke test performed on staging cluster.
upgrade_instructions: 1) Configure object store and KMS key in installer config; 2) Run 'redwood-installer backup --output=latest' before upgrade; 3) Run 'redwood-installer upgrade --target-version=v1.9.0' (for unsafe downgrades, document requires '--allow-downgrade' and an explicit migration plan); 4) If post-upgrade verification fails, run 'redwood-installer restore --snapshot=latest'
notes_for_ops: Operators: backups are disabled by default for air-gapped installs. If you enable hooks, ensure installer has IAM/S3 access and KMS decrypt permissions. Check snapshot_metadata in Terraform outputs for the expected S3 key format. Downgrades will be blocked unless reverse migrations exist or '--allow-downgrade' is supplied with documented mitigations.
